newsitem.title: UK: Utd Utilities up on tax hopes, Schroder push.
newsitem.headline: Utd Utilities up on tax hopes, Schroder push.

text.p: Shares in United Utilities Plc led water stocks higher on Thursday as press reports suggested Labour's planned windfall tax will be lower than some expected and analysts at Schroders recommended the sector, dealers said.
Analyst Michael Cohen at Schroders confirmed he had issued a "buy" note on the sector but declined further comment.

United Utilities was up 14p at 657-1/2 by 0945 GMT and other water stocks also rose with Thames Water Plc up 8p at 679, Yorkshire Water Plc up 10p at 364, Severn Trent Plc up 15-1/2 at 734-1/2 and Hyder Plc up 14p at 830.

A report on the Financial Times said the opposition Labour Party, likely to win an election to be held on May 1, was still undecided on how much money would be raised from the windfall tax on privatised utilities.
The tax is planned to fund a programme of training and job-creation schemes.
The FT said Labour leader Tony Blair wanted to limit the overall amount raised to between three billion stg and five billion, less than had been sought by prospective finance minister Gordon Brown.
Separately a report in the Times newspaper on how the tax would be set concluded that Labour could spread the tax more thinly across a wide range of companies.
"The water sector was bashed down to lower ratings on fears of how severe the windfall tax would be," said one market marker. "Maybe these reports have been a more calming influence."
United Utilities for instance touched a three-month low of 603p at the end of March, after dropping in the days after Prime Minister John Major set the election date on March 17.
